newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S MBEKI PLANS SIX-NATION TOUR OVER ZAIRE.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S MBEKI PLANS SIX-NATION TOUR OVER ZAIRE.

text.p: South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki will start on Wednesday a six-nation African tour, including a visit to Zaire, to try keep peace efforts on track there, the Foreign Affairs department said.
"It is hoped that during these visits, agreement will be reached on the way forward, through broad consultation," it said in a statement on Tuesday.
Mbeki held an hour-long meeting with U.S. envoy Bill Richardson in Cape Town on Tuesday to discuss their efforts to mediate in Zaire's civil war.
Richardson said afterwards that diplomatic efforts to avoid a bloody showdown in Kinshasa were still on track.

Mbeki's tour is one of a number of rounds of regional diplomacy aimed at averting a bloody takeover of Kinshasa by rebel leader Laurent Kabila's forces, which have gained control of three-quarters of Zaire in their seven-month-old campaign to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko.
Mbeki will start his tour in Angola, after which he will visit Tanzania and Rwanda before arriving in Zaire on Friday.
He is scheduled to visit Kabila's stronghold Lubumbashi and Kinshasa on Friday, then proceed to Congo and Gabon on Saturday before returning to South Africa the same day.
In the past week, Richardson has held talks with Mobutu, Kabila and the leaders of most of Zaire's nine neighbours, which would be threatened by the collapse of the vast central African state.
Mobutu will travel to Gabon on Wednesday to meet other heads of state, returning to Kinshasa two days later, on a trip linked to the international mediation in Zaire, his spokesman said on Tuesday.
He did not specify whom Mobutu would meetin Gabon, whose President Omar Bongo has been on close terms with Mobutu for three decades.
